edit.description: `frictionNotes` and `countFrictionFiles` take the root their dir descends from, the shape `listUnderStateRoot` (`harness/dirListing.ts`) already has
`frictionFiles` hands down the state root it already holds
`status`'s three presence guards and `loop`'s start refusal prove the descent from the root each holds before reading absence as silence
the listing's absence arm over an obstructed root
the status lines' and the loop refusal's obstructed-root readings

summary: `flume status`'s three presence lines, `loop`'s start refusal and the friction listing each read absence off one stat, so an obstructed ancestor prints nothing and lists empty
acceptance: every arm that reads an absent artifact as silence proves the descent from a root it holds — `flume status`'s supervisor, stop-flag and tip-claim lines, `flume loop`'s stop-flag refusal, and the friction channel's one listing — so a present-but-unreachable artifact refuses on every host rather than reading as nothing there
pins: flume status refuses a loop lock whose state root is present and is not a directory
the friction listing refuses a state root that is present and is not a directory rather than listing empty
notes: Verified this tick: `existsLoud` (`src/fsProbe.ts`) declares the win32 bound and names the descent a cross-host absence needs, so the probe is a declared divergence and this files against its callers — `src/cli.ts:350`, `:386`, `:419`, `:1198` — plus `frictionNotes` (`src/friction.ts:90`). `frictionCountLine` and `frictionFiles` already hold the root; only the inner two lack it. No `tests[]`: posix raises ENOTDIR and every arm throws on it today, so the `windows` lane is what the pins protect.
